analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is a subscale wind O&M services business with 1% ROE, flat-to-declining revenue over seven years, and profits already shrinking after just turning positive — yet it trades at 81x P/E and 129x EV/EBITDA. I would not pay this price for a wonderful business; this is neither wonderful nor cheap.
key_strengths: Debt dramatically reduced from INR 1,411 Cr (2021) to INR 95 Cr (2025), nearly debt-free now
Captive O&M pipeline tied to Inox Wind's installed base provides revenue visibility
Operating margin of ~15% is reasonable for a services business
key_risks: Valuation is absurd: market pays INR 6,549 Cr for a business earning INR 22 Cr — P/E of 81x is pricing in decades of flawless execution
Revenue has gone nowhere in 7 years (INR 368 Cr in 2018 → INR 236 Cr in 2025, CAGR -6.1%); net profit is already declining after just two profitable years
1% ROE and 2.6% ROCE mean the business destroys economic value at current asset base; massive equity dilution (equity grew 47x since 2021) has not translated to proportionate earnings
red_flags: Profits declining immediately after turning positive: INR 28 Cr (2024) → INR 22 Cr (2025)
INR 637 Cr investing outflow in 2025 funded by INR 572 Cr new financing — major capital raise being deployed into a business with sub-3% ROCE
Other Income swung from -INR 112 Cr (2021) to +INR 57 Cr (2025), masking weak operating performance; earnings quality is suspect
Subsidiary of Inox Wind — related-party captive model limits true market validation and pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inox Green is essentially a captive wind farm O&M operator for its parent, Inox Wind. The core business has generated roughly INR 160–250 Cr in revenue for the past seven years with no real growth — the 7-year revenue CAGR is negative at -6.1%. EBITDA is contracting (INR 128 Cr in 2020 vs. INR 94 Cr in 2025). The company only turned profitable in FY24, and profits are already falling. ROE of 1% and ROCE of 2.6% tell me this business earns far less than its cost of capital — a value-destruction machine dressed up in a green-energy narrative.

The valuation is indefensible by any framework I use. At INR 6,549 Cr market cap on INR 22 Cr of net profit (P/E 81x) and INR 236 Cr revenue (P/S 22x), the market is pricing in a transformation that the historical numbers give no reason to believe in. The 2025 balance sheet shows a massive fresh capital raise (equity jumped from INR 1,345 Cr to INR 2,020 Cr) being deployed into INR 637 Cr of investments — but into a business that has never demonstrated the ability to earn adequate returns. This is speculative capital allocation, not a business I'd trust with Berkshire's shareholders' money.
